Rule: Facilities & bases are physical game pieces
Description: Facilities & bases are physical installations represented by game pieces and placed on the map. They are subject to territorial control and physical game interactions.
The system contains distinct facility types with individually defined functions, including Research Facilities and Bases.
Research Facilities are physical infrastructure analogous in principle to Industrial Complexes and can be subject to strategic bombing and damage.

Bases are military installations providing operational capabilities. It is physical infrastructure analogous in principle to Airfields and Naval Bases and provide their individually defined operational effects.
Research Centres are identified separately as `RCENTER` and constitute a specialised facility class within the data model.
A Research Centre may be required for eligibility to research specific technologies.
Facilities other than Research Centres do not themselves function as prerequisites for researching technologies.
A technology may unlock the ability to build or purchase a specific facility or base.
Unlocking a facility gives the player the ability to build or purchase it, it does not automatically place the physical facility on the map.
If a facility unlocked by Technology A enables a later technological development, the later technology depends on Technology A rather than on possession of the physical facility.
The gameplay effect of a facility is determined by its individual rules/description rather than by a universal facility effect.
Facilities can be damaged by applicable game effects, including strategic bombing, according to their individual rules.
Damage affects the operational capability of a facility according to its rules.
Damaging or disabling a facility does not remove the technology that unlocked it.
Facilities are associated with the territory in which they are located and are subject to applicable ownership/capture rules.
The technological unlock, purchase/construction, placement, and subsequent operation of a facility are separate game events.
Facilities do not inherently generate Research Points merely because they are facilities. RP generation must be explicitly defined by the facility's own rules.
A Research Centre may provide RP or other research-related effects when explicitly specified by its individual rules.
Possession or loss of a physical facility does not change whether its associated technology has been researched.
Facility type, category, unlock relationship, description, and other properties should be represented in the canonical data rather than hardcoded into visualisation logic.
Each facility has its own purchase/build cost. The cost is determined independently from the technology's research cost and may reflect the strategic power and usefulness of the facility.
More powerful, specialised, or strategically significant facilities may have higher costs than more ordinary facilities.

Rule: Technology cost and facility cost are separate
Description: Researching a technology and subsequently constructing/purchasing a facility it unlocks are separate economic decisions with separate costs.

A facility unlocked by a technology is represented as a physical game piece rather than as a separate technology node. A facility should not be duplicated as a technology solely to represent a dependency.
A territory may contain at most one facility of each facility type.
Facilities and Bases are both physical installations. Facilities can be targeted by Strategic Bombing raids. Bases can be targeted by both Tactical Bombing and Strategic Bombing raids.

A base is considered inoperative if it has 3 or more damage points. Damage reduces or disables the base's abilities according to the applicable base rules, those abilities return as the damage is repaired.
When a Research Centre is first purchased, it immediately unlocks access to the applicable Tier 4+ technologies and provides a one-time establishment bonus appropriate to its research domain.
